Article Title: What's in a name? Pakistan boxer's hate for 'Narendra'
Article Text:
Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him.

NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer who had "started hating" the name 'Narendra' after discovering that his Indian opponent, his coach and India's PM all shared the name drew laughs as Narendra Modi interacted with India's Commonwealth Games medallists Sunday.Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him. "Bhaijan, aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai. Mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai," Berwal recalled, triggering laughter from Modi and the athletes.Modi particularly lauded Lovlina Borgohain, silver medallist in the women's 75kg boxing event, for raising a map issue on the final day of the Glasgow Games. The Indian contingent had gone out to celebrate when she had noticed that a map of India at the restaurant did not show the North-East. Lovlina said she brought the error to the attention of the restaurant staff, following which they agreed to correct it.Modi said the fact that she noticed and acted on it even in the middle of celebrations made the gesture significant and one that would be remembered for a long time.Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, who won gold in the women's 48kg category, provided one of the more emotional moments.Modi asked her about the tears she shed on the podium after her victory.She said the medal came after four difficult years marked by injuries, family problems and the disappointment of missing a medal at the Paris Olympics by just one kilogram. "When our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, we cannot stop ourselves," she told Modi, explaining why she broke down on the podium.Modi told the medallists that their performances were capable of drawing far more children towards sport than campaigns alone. "Your medal inspires them more than anything we could say by going to schools," he said.
Article Summary: Pakistani boxer Narender Berwal had "started hating" the name 'Narendra' after discovering that his Indian opponent, his coach and India's PM all shared the name. Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him.

Article Title: On camera: Swollen river sweeps away bridge after flash flood in Uttarakhand's Chamoli
Article Text:
Bridge damaged after Tamak drain overflows in Chamoli

NEW DELHI: A bridge over the Tamak drain beyond Malari in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district was swept away after the drain overflowed amid a strong water current, disrupting traffic in the area on Monday.No casualties have been reported so far.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed officials to prioritise relief and rescue efforts, ensure the safety of people in vulnerable areas and maintain supplies of essential commodities to affected villages through alternative routes, if needed.Police, district administration, SDRF and NDRF teams have been deployed to the spot, while authorities continue to monitor the situation."There is a Tamak Nala, and a very strong surge of water occurred there this evening at 5.30pm. A Bailey bridge at the site was washed away; BRO officials and staff were present in the immediate vicinity. A BRO vehicle and its driver have gone missing," news agency ANI quoted Chamoli additional district magistrate (ADM) Vivek Prakash saying."A search operation is underway, and an SDRF team has been dispatched to the site. About 15 or 16 villages are located on the other side of the bridge; we are making urgent efforts to restore connectivity so that services can be resumed by tomorrow," he added.
Article Summary: A bridge over the Tamak drain beyond Malari in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district was swept away after the drain overflowed amid a strong water current. No casualties have been reported so far. Police, district administration, SDRF and NDRF teams have been deployed to the spot.

Article Title: In a first on I-Day this time, ‘Vande Mataram’ will be sung before nat’l anthem from Red Fort; ‘Yuva Shakti’ will be on full display, LOP will be seated at per table of precedence: Defence secy
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For the first time at the Independence Day function at Red Fort this year, Vande Mataram will be sung and over 27,000 dignitaries, visitors and students will have to stand during the playing of the national song, defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said on Monday. Besides Vande Mataram, Yuva Shakti will be on full display on Aug 15.Addressing a briefing here, the defence secretary said, “As 2026 marks 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, the national song that inspired millions during the freedom struggle will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time as a tribute to its enduring legacy. The sequence (of events) is that he (PM Modi) arrives on the rampart, then the national song is played and everybody keeps standing. Thereafter, he unfurls the flag and the national anthem is played. ” The floral decoration will showcase ‘Vande Mataram’, with a total of 2,500 boy and girl cadets of NCC and ‘My Bharat’ volunteers forming Vande Mataram’ on Gyanpath opposite the rampart. An IAF Mi-17 helicopter will carry a banner commemorating 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, and shower flower petals at the venue.The I-Day celebrations 2026 will also acknowledge the success of youth in different spheres.Achievements of 19 medal-winning students in international physics, chemistry, biology and mathematical Olympiad 2026 is an example of the success of Yuva Shakti in the field of science. “They have been invited for the function and will be seated on the rampart,” the defence secretary said, adding, “over 500 students from Delhi govt schools have also been invited for the event. ”When asked whether ‘Yuva Shakti: Leading the journey to Viksit Bharat @2047’ theme was decided after the Jantar Mantar student protest, Singh said, “Such big celebrations are planned much in advance. It was planned much before the protests.”When asked about a controversy in the past involving Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s seating arrangement, the defence secretary said, “In the past, his seat was assigned as per the table of precedence. This year too, LOP has been invited, and his seating would be as per the table of precedence, which is exactly after Cabinet ministers.”View cutters in the backdrop will showcase India’s progress in nuclear and space technology, with the floral decoration at the guard of honour area depicting India’s journey to Viksit Bharat in 2047. Around 5,000 special guests, who are achievers from different walks of life and are guiding the country in its Viksit Bharat journey, have been invited as special guests for the celebrations. Special guests also include the silent warriors, who work hard round-the-clock to assist others in achieving their goals.For I-Day celebrations, the names of the seating enclosures have been named after major lakes of India.Over 1,500 Delhi-based people from various states/UTs dressed in traditional attire have also been invited to witness the grand ceremony. Paying tribute to the anthem that united and inspired generations during the freedom struggle, a number of band performances are being held pan-India from Aug 8.Delhi Metro will be operational from 4 am on Aug 15 for people to reach the venue. Metro services will be provided free of cost to all invitees. Metro QR codes will be provided with e-invitation.
Article Summary: For the first time at the Independence Day function at Red Fort this year, Vande Mataram will be sung. Over 27,000 dignitaries, visitors and students will have to stand during the playing of the national song. Yuva Shakti will be on full display on Aug 15.

Article Title: Search ops involving Indian Navy for 3 missing fishermen continue in Kerala: Official
Article Text:
INS Kalpeni sailed from Kochi on Saturday night to join the search operation and anchored one nautical mile off Neendakara on Sunday morning (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: A search operation involving the Indian Navy for three fishermen who went missing following separate boat mishaps off Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram coasts will continue on Monday, a defence spokesperson has said.The search operation for Gautam Krishna, John and Shijin -- who went missing in separate fishing boat mishaps at Neendakara (in Kollam), Vizhinjam and Muthalappozhi (in Thiruvananthapuram), respectively, on July 31 -- entered its 10th day on Sunday.On Sunday, Indian Navy divers joined the Coast Police, Coast Guard and Marine Enforcement Wing of the fisheries department to search for the three missing fishermen.INS Kalpeni sailed from Kochi on Saturday night to join the search operation and anchored one nautical mile off Neendakara on Sunday morning, the spokesperson said.The divers are using portable SONAR, which enhances their capability for underwater surveillance and diving operations, the spokesperson said. The Navy initially focused its search on Gautam Krishna, who went missing after his fishing boat capsized off the Neendakara coast. Later in the evening, INS Kalpeni moved to Muthalappozhi harbour to continue the search.
Article Summary: The search operation for Gautam Krishna, John and Shijin entered its 10th day on Sunday. Indian Navy divers joined the Coast Police, Coast Guard and Marine Enforcement Wing of the fisheries department to search for the three missing fishermen. The divers are using portable SONAR, which enhances their capability for underwater surveillance and diving operations.

Article Title: Afghanistan qualify for 2027 ODI World Cup after thrilling win over Ireland
Article Text:
Image credit: ACB

Rashid, Ahmadzai take Afghanistan home

Afghanistan secure World Cup spot

Rahmat Shah praises bowling effort

NEW DELHI: Afghanistan secured direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup after beating Ireland by three wickets in the third ODI at the Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast on Monday. The win also gave Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match series.Afghanistan bowled Ireland out for 206 in 46.3 overs before chasing down the target in 44.5 overs. The win was set up by a strong bowling effort and a calm finish from Rashid Khan.Afghanistan entered the third ODI knowing that a win would be enough to seal their place in the 2027 ODI World Cup. They had already beaten Ireland by 92 runs in the second ODI, while the opening match of the five-match series was washed out.Afghanistan looked in control at 97 for two during the chase but lost five wickets for 79 runs to slip to 176 for seven.Rashid then stepped up when his team needed him most. He remained unbeaten on 37 off 43 balls, hitting four boundaries, while Yamin Ahmadzai stayed not out on four off 26 balls.The pair held their nerve to take Afghanistan across the finish line without any further damage.Rashid was named Player of the Match for his crucial contribution.Afghanistan, currently ranked No. 8 in ODIs, have now secured direct qualification for the 2027 World Cup, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.This will be Afghanistan's fourth appearance in an ODI World Cup.Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah credited his bowlers for sticking to their plans and adapting quickly to the conditions."Thank you. It was a low-scoring match, always tough. Finally, we won the match."On Afghanistan's bowling performance, he said: "Yeah, I give them the plans according to the field, according to the situation, and they read very well, especially Yamin Ahmadzai bowled really well, Rashid and Ghanzafar, they bowled really well too. They bowled according to the field, and especially they assessed the conditions early."Rahmat said Afghanistan's chase was challenging because of the low-scoring nature of the game."Of course, yes, because always a low-scoring match is very tough, and finally we won the match."He also pointed out the ninth-wicket partnership that helped Ireland post a competitive total and said Afghanistan would look to break such partnerships earlier in future."I think the ninth-wicket partnership, Ireland did very well. Inshallah, we try to break these partnerships early if we are in a good situation on that time. Inshallah, we will try our best."
Article Summary: Afghanistan secure direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup after beating Ireland by three wickets in the third ODI. The win also gave Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match series. Afghanistan bowled Ireland out for 206 in 46.3 overs before chasing down the target in 44.5 overs.

Article Title: 'Meri galti nahi thi': Harbhajan Singh reveals why he was expelled from NCA - WATCH

NEW DELHI: Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh has opened up about an incident that led to his expulsion from the National Cricket Academy (NCA) in Bengaluru in 2000.Harbhajan, who was among the first group of trainees at the NCA, recalled how he tore up a diet chart after repeatedly complaining that the food being served did not match the prescribed diet. He said the incident was later used as the reason for his removal.Harbhajan said the NCA had a fixed diet plan for its trainees, but the food served did not follow the chart. According to him, repeated complaints did not lead to any change.The former India spinner said his frustration eventually boiled over and he tore the diet chart."Waha se mujhe nikaal diya gaya. Woh meri galti nahi thi. Main aaj bhi is baat ko khule aam kehta hoon, kyunki woh hamara haq tha. Jo hamara khaana tha, woh achha nahi tha. [They removed me from there. It was not my mistake, I say this openly even today. It was our right. The food was not good there]," the former India spinner said on cricketnextofficial."Wahan jo rules aur regulations the, woh yahi the ki humein bahut kuch padhaya ja raha tha, sikhaya ja raha tha. Ek chart lagaya tha, jismein tha ki ye diet honi chahiye, expert ki diet ke hisaab se humein woh diet milni chahiye.Lekin woh khaana mil nahi raha tha. [Back then, the rules and regulations were such that we were told and taught a lot, and a chart was put up for the diet. But we were not getting food as per that diet. Despite complaining many times, the food did not improve. So one day I tore that chart. This was my only mistake, that I tore the chart]" Harbhajan said.Harbhajan said he believed his decision to speak up was necessary because the problems with the diet plan would not have been addressed otherwise."But maybe till someone does something like this, things don't change. I was fighting for the rights. If I had not stood up, even today the same diet plan would have been followed. The plan changed, I was also removed, that is a different thing, but it was not my fault. There were some people in the BCCI who did not want someone who could stand up and question them," Harbhajan added.ID@undefinedCaption not available.ID@undefinedCaption not available.ID@undefinedCaption not available.Harbhajan went on to become one of India's most successful spinners. He represented India from 1998 to 2016 and finished his international career with more than 700 wickets across formats.He played 103 Tests and took 417 wickets, including 25 five-wicket hauls and five 10-wicket match hauls.In 236 ODIs, Harbhajan claimed 269 wickets, including three five-wicket hauls. He also played 28 T20Is and took 25 wickets.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh has opened up about an incident that led to his expulsion from the National Cricket Academy (NCA) in Bengaluru in 2000. He recalled how he tore up a diet chart after repeatedly complaining that the food being served did not match the prescribed diet. He said the incident was later used as the reason for his removal.

Article Title: Sarfaraz Khan's return: A 17kg weight loss, relentless fight and a Test recall
Article Text:
Sarfaraz Khan (AP Photo)

Shedding weight

Sarfaraz Khan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In cricket, as in life, fortunes can change in a short time. Over the years, Sarfaraz Khan has subtly expressed his frustration at being sidelined from the Indian Test team despite consistent performances in the Ranji Trophy On Friday, the Mumbai batter posted a photo on Instagram from the 2019 Telugu film ‘Jersey’ with a caption that read: “I may not fit in, but I’ll fight with everything I’ve got.”Just 48 hours later, the 28-yearold was rewarded for his seemingly endless ‘fight’ when he replaced the injured Sai Sudharsan in the Indian squad for the Test series against Sri Lanka. After finally receiving the news he had been waiting for, Sarfaraz shared his first post on social media, posting a couple of pictures in the Team India travelling jersey. On Monday, Sarfaraz was the cynosure of all eyes as he practiced with the Indian team in Colombo.On eve of Sarfaraz’s departure, Sarfaraz’s father-cum-coach Naushad Khan , who has a penchant for shayari when he’s not coaching his kids, posted a reel where he tells his cricketer sons Sarfaraz and Musheer Khan that luck favours hardwork.The Test recall, which has come after 19 months in the wilderness for Sarfaraz, marks a heartening comeback of a man who was last year ignored by the national selectors even for the India A home series against South Africa A ahead of the Proteas’ tour of India, based on the logic that they had “seen enough” of him and wanted to try the others too.With the three-day warm-up game in Colombo having concluded on Sunday, Sarfaraz will look to make the most of the practice sessions to prepare for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka.One of the criticisms against Sarfaraz was that he was overweight. Many deemed him unfit to play toplevel cricket, even though legendary opener Sunil Gavaskar countered that by saying that a player’s performance and cricket fitness are more important than their body weight. In a heartening development that has certainly helped him in his cricket career, Sarfaraz, before being picked for the India A squad for the upcoming tour of England last year, eventually decided to improve on this aspect too.After remaining unsold in the IPL for two years before the Chennai Super Kings bought him in IPL-2026 auction, he worked hard on improving his fitness in recent times, and shedding excess weight. The Mumbaikar has lost a staggering 17 kgs in a year’s time and now bears a much trimmer, fitter look. In fact, since 2025, Sarfaraz’s whole family has been on a weightlosing spree which has produced significant results. Advised to lose weight on an urgent basis to avoid a knee replacement surgery, Naushad Khan lost 12 kgs in a month last year.“Our whole family is focused on a weight-losing mission. Sarfaraz has lost nine kilograms too in six weeks, which isn’t easy, and he’s raring to lose more weight. Both Sarfaraz and I have been slogging in the gym for at least an hour for six days a week. I go for a walk, while he jogs for almost an hour, and then there’s a 30-minute swimming session. Even my younger son Moin (Khan) has lost a lot of weight,” Naushad had told TOI.Much of this weight loss mission for the Khans also involved a strict diet. “Sarfaraz and I have stopped eating atta (flour) and rice at home completely. Our diet is now strict but interesting — we eat sauteed vegetable with boiled chicken, boiled eggs, and drink green tea and black coffee. We are using little (olive) oil in our food,” Naushad had revealed.It meant that Sarfaaz was no longer feasting on his favourite non-vegetarian dishes — particularly biryani — but it’s a sacrifice that the middleorder batter consciously made to improve his fitness drastically.
Article Summary: Sarfaraz Khan replaced the injured Sai Sudharsan in the Indian squad for the Test series against Sri Lanka. The Test recall comes after 19 months in the wilderness for Sarfaraz. The Mumbaikar has lost a staggering 17 kgs in a year’s time and now bears a much trimmer, fitter look.

Article Title: Why John Cena's WWE contract prohibits him from wrestling elsewhere even after retiring from in-ring competition

John Cena may have officially stepped away from in-ring competition, but his relationship with WWE is far from over. This is because, in a recent interview, the 17-time World Champion addressed the possibility of returning to the ring after the company approached him even after his retirement. The WWE legend indicated that it would make little financial sense for anyone to convince him to compete again, suggesting that only an extraordinary financial offer could potentially change his mind.Though Cena has always maintained that his active professional wrestling is over, he appeared as an official host at WrestleMania 42 in 2026, which took place at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Meanwhile, a recent report suggests that WWE has prohibited him from wrestling anywhere even after his retirement. But what is the reason behind this WWE contract? Let’s find out more about it. WWE legend John Cena may have retired from in-ring competition, but the Cenation Leader remains tied exclusively to WWE. According to a recent PWMania report citing Fightful Select, Cena’s new WWE contract prohibits him from wrestling for another promotion.The agreement was signed ahead of his retirement and reportedly shifted Cena into an ambassadorial role with WWE. With this move, WWE has retained him under a long-term agreement that keeps him connected to the company while preventing any potential appearance with another company.Besides, Cena has remained one of the most recognizable faces in wrestling history, and his association with WWE carries substantial promotional value. Even without wrestling, he can represent the company at major events, participate in promotional activities, and remain part of WWE's broader brand strategy.In addition to this, Cena made it clear he's not walking away from wrestling and revealed that he's still finding different ways to contribute behind the scenes. He further revealed that he is currently mentoring talent and staying engaged with the company through organizational work. Further, Cena said that he is interested in contributing to WWE's long-term growth and helping shape its future.Cena was last seen at the WWE Backlash 2026 Premium Live Event in May, where he made an announcement that was promised to shock the WWE Universe with the introduction of the "John Cena Classic," a tournament designed to pit the current WWE roster against up-and-coming stars, but there has been no further information since Cena's appearance at Backlash.Reports suggest the John Cena Classic is still planned for later this year, with a target date in December, although this has not been finalized yet.It is to be noted that the 17-time World Champion wrestled his final match at last December’s Saturday Night’s Main Event, where he faced “The Ring General” GUNTHER, and will now be focused on his WWE ambassadorial responsibilities rather than another championship run or a surprise return to competition.
Article Summary: WWE legend John Cena may have retired from in-ring competition, but the Cenation Leader remains tied exclusively to WWE. According to a recent PWMania report, Cena’s new WWE contract prohibits him from wrestling for another promotion. The agreement was signed ahead of his retirement and reportedly shifted Cena into an ambassadorial role with WWE.

Article Title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' marriage keeps "breaking up" online, and it's never because of anything they actually did
Article Text:
Brittany Mahomes opens up about their marriage.(Image via Getty Images)

Why Patrick and Brittany Mahomes can't escape marriage trouble rumors, no matter what they do

"resting b***h face."

"Man people are weird... love you babe"

"sad how disrespectful some women are"

"not going to disturb my peace"

Why the "shut it down" strategy never actually works

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There's a version of fame where nothing you do is neutral. Sit apart at a game, you're clearly divorcing. Sit together and smile, you're clearly overcompensating. That's the box Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have been stuck in for years now, and the latest round proves it hasn't gotten any less absurd or any less exhausting for two people who've been together since high school.At the FIFA World Cup quarterfinals on July 11, cameras panned to the Mahomes' luxury box at Arrowhead and caught something apparently scandalous: Patrick, seated a row behind Brittany, looking at his phone. That was it. That was the whole incident.Journalist Danilo Lacalle called it "weird" on X, another post joked "BREAKING: married couple gets into argument," and from there the algorithm did what it does. Someone else declared the body language "not happy marriage behavior," and a comparison to Donald and Melania Trump's famously frosty public dynamic started making the rounds too.What actually undercuts the panic, if anyone bothered to check: Patrick and Brittany had attended JuJu Smith-Schuster's wedding together just one day earlier, and by all accounts looked like they were having a great time. Nobody screenshotted that.If this were an isolated moment, it'd barely be worth writing about. It's not. The Mahomes' have been fending off "trouble in paradise" narratives for years, and the receipts pile up fast:Back in 2022, viral footage from a Texas Tech game showed Patrick saying something to Brittany that left her visibly stunned, prompting one X account to claim he'd told her to fix herPatrick addressed it obliquely on Twitter, saying,without ever confirming what was actually said.By 2024, actual body language analysts were being brought in by gossip outlets to dissect the couple's posture in red carpet clips, with one expert describing Patrick's reach for Brittany's hand as "stiff" and "obligatory" rather than affectionate, and reading Brittany's turned head as a sign she wanted distance. This is, to be clear, a professional interpreting a few seconds of hallway footage between two people who've been together for over a decade.There's also a persistent infidelity thread that never fully goes away. In 2023, Brittany addressed rumors about other women pursuing Patrick directly in an Instagram Q&A, calling itand insisting they werewhile admitting it used to bother her more than she let on. That admission, meant to shut the topic down, arguably kept it alive; it gave people a real quote to keep recirculating every time a new rumor cycle starts.Now, beyond the usual gossip churn, the Mahomes' have tried the obvious counter-move, repeatedly, and it never lands the way they'd want.Eight days after the World Cup seating drama, at the tournament final between Spain and Argentina, Brittany posted a run of Instagram Stories from their suite before kickoff, and the couple was photographed all smiles watching the match together. It read almost too clearly as a rebuttal. They ran the same play back at the F1 Miami Grand Prix in 2025, holding hands for the cameras in the middle of an earlier round of split chatter.The problem is the logic has no exit. Distant photos get read as evidence of a crack. Happy photos get read as evidence they're covering for the crack. A body language expert can find something "off" in either one if that's the assignment.There is no photo that proves a marriage is fine to an audience that's already decided otherwise, which means the "shut it down" strategy was never actually going to work, because it was never really about proof to begin with. It's about a couple famous enough that any unremarkable moment gets filled in with a plot.Patrick and Brittany started dating in high school in 2012, got engaged at Arrowhead in 2020 right after his first Super Bowl ring ceremony, married in Maui in 2022, and now have three kids together. That's over a decade of actual, verifiable history. Neither of them has directly addressed this latest round of speculation, or really any round before it, and at this point, that silence might be the closest thing to a tell we're going to get: not that something is wrong, but that they've stopped expecting a rumor mill this committed to being right to ever actually be talked out of it.
Article Summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have been dogged by marriage rumors for years. They've tried the obvious counter-move, repeatedly, and it never lands the way they'd want. Neither of them has directly addressed this latest round of speculation, and at this point, that might be the closest thing to a thing to being right.

Article Title: Khabib Nurmagomedov and Conor McGregor feud: Daniel Cormier explains why they could never make peace like Jon Jones

Daniel Cormier has explained why Khabib Nurmagomedov could not handle his bitter rivalry with Conor McGregor in the same way Cormier eventually handled his feud with Jon Jones. Cormier believes the key difference is family, faith and loyalty. He said McGregor crossed a personal line that made peace much harder for Nurmagomedov, while Cormier and Jones eventually found a way to work together despite years of bad blood.Cormier discussed the rivalry during an interview with. Having trained alongside Nurmagomedov and his team, he said he understands how seriously they take family, religion and loyalty to the people around them.That is why Cormier does not think Nurmagomedov could simply put the McGregor feud behind him. He said the former UFC lightweight champion and his brothers would see some of McGregor’s actions as something much more personal than normal fight talk.“I know my brothers, and I know how committed they are to their religion, their faith and their family,” Cormier said.Cormier then looked at his own history with Jones. Their rivalry was one of the most heated in UFC history, but their relationship later became more workable.The two have since appeared together and worked in the same setting, something Cormier believes would be difficult for Nurmagomedov and McGregor.He also pointed to a difference in how people from different backgrounds may deal with conflict. Cormier said his team had strong feelings about Jones too, but they were able to move forward. He added that Americans can have different beliefs and ways of dealing with these situations.For Cormier, McGregor’s behavior went beyond what he could accept as ordinary promotion. He described it as “bad” and said that was the reason McGregor no longer has a relationship with the people around Nurmagomedov.The point is not that Cormier thinks his rivalry with Jones was less serious. Instead, he believes the two situations had different personal limits, which is why the endings could also be different.Ian Machado Garry has taken a different part of the debate by defending Nurmagomedov’s decision to leave MMA while McGregor has criticized the former champion’s retirement.Speaking to, Garry said Nurmagomedov should be judged on what he achieved rather than what he might have done if he had continued fighting. He called him “one of the greatest fighters we’ve ever seen.”Garry also pointed to Nurmagomedov’s 29-0 professional record and UFC championship. For him, those achievements are enough to explain why the Russian remains among the sport’s best, even though his career ended earlier than some fans expected.“Khabib stopped fighting for something much more important than fighting,” Garry said.Garry’s argument is simple: a fighter does not need to continue until every possible question about his career is answered. Nurmagomedov chose to leave, and his record remains unbeaten.His comments also give more context to Cormier’s explanation. While Cormier focused on why the McGregor feud became so personal, Garry focused on why Nurmagomedov’s decision to walk away should not change how his career is remembered.
Article Summary: Daniel Cormier has explained why Khabib Nurmagomedov could not handle his bitter rivalry with Conor McGregor. Cormier believes the key difference is family, faith and loyalty. He said McGregor crossed a personal line that made peace much harder. Ian Machado Garry has taken a different part of the debate by defending the Russian’s decision to leave MMA.

Article Title: Tim Anderson retires after 10 MLB seasons as former White Sox star opens up about his difficult final years
Article Text:
Tim Anderson retires after 10 MLB seasons as former White Sox star opens up about his difficult final years

Tim Anderson explains why he is retiring after 10 MLB seasons

Chicago White Sox to honor Tim Anderson in September

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tim Anderson is retiring from Major League Baseball after 10 seasons. The former Chicago White Sox shortstop, who won the 2019 American League batting title and made two All-Star teams, announced the decision Monday at age 33. Anderson said he tried to get his body back to where it once was, but could not. His last MLB appearance came with the Los Angeles Angels on May 25, 2025.Anderson spent eight seasons with the White Sox before playing for the Miami Marlins and Angels. Across 991 games, he hit .276 with 98 home runs, 350 RBIs and 122 stolen bases. He became one of Chicago’s most recognizable players during his best years and won the batting title in 2019 after hitting .335.His two All-Star selections came in 2021 and 2022. Anderson also won a Silver Slugger Award in 2020. One of his biggest moments came in the 2021 Field of Dreams game, when he hit a walk-off home run against the New York Yankees.The later part of his career was much harder. Injuries limited him, and his production fell after his strong run with Chicago. He joined Miami in 2024 and later signed with Los Angeles for the 2025 season.The Angels designated him for assignment in May 2025, and he did not return to the majors.Anderson said the physical side was only part of the reason. “I fought for the last two, three years. You know, I trained and I just couldn’t get the body to operate like it used to,” he said, according to The Associated Press.He also spoke about how difficult baseball had become for him mentally. “It just got to the point where I really couldn’t enjoy it,” Anderson said. “Just being in that setting, it just wasn’t the same.”The White Sox plan to honor Anderson before their Sept. 17 game against the Detroit Tigers. The team will wear its black-and-white Nike City Connect “Southside” uniforms for the only time this season.The uniforms carry a special link to Anderson’s White Sox years. He wore them during the team’s 2021 season, when Chicago won the American League Central. The tribute gives the former shortstop a chance to return to the place where he spent most of his career.Anderson’s time in baseball also included painful moments away from the field. A close friend was shot and killed in Alabama in 2017, and Anderson later spoke publicly about how that affected him. In a 2023 appearance on The Pivot Podcast, he also discussed personal problems in his marriage and said he and his wife, Bria, went through therapy.Now, Anderson is stepping away after a career that included major awards, memorable games and difficult stretches. His decision comes after a long effort to continue playing, but he said he reached a point where the game no longer felt the same.
Article Summary: Tim Anderson won the 2019 American League batting title and made two All-Star teams. Anderson said he tried to get his body back to where it once was, but could not. His last MLB appearance came with the Los Angeles Angels on May 25, 2025.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My brother and I came from nothing. I fight for my family.”- How Jake Paul turned internet controversy and relentless work ethic into boxing stardom
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My brother and I came from nothing. I fight for my family.”- How Jake Paul turned internet controversy and relentless work ethic into boxing stardom

Jake Paul and Logan Paul started out together in Ohio

Jake Paul turned internet fame into a boxing career

Jake Paul has built a career that goes far beyond the videos that first made him famous. The Ohio-born creator moved from Vine and YouTubeinto professional boxing, where he has faced former MMA champions, a former NBA player and Mike Tyson . His rise has also come with plenty of criticism, but boxing gave him a new way to build his identity. At the centre of that journey has been his family, especially older brother Logan Paul . Their shared start in Ohio and years in the public eye help explain why Jake often links his success to the people closest to him.Before Jake Paul became a boxer, he was known mainly as an internet personality. He grew up in Westlake, Ohio, with his older brother Logan Paul. Their parents are Greg Paul and Pam Stepnick. Both brothers became interested in sports and making videos while they were young, eventually turning that interest into careers.The brothers later moved toward Los Angeles as their online careers grew. Jake became known for prank and stunt-based content, while Logan also built a large following. Their early success came through platforms such as Vine and YouTube, long before either brother became closely linked with combat sports.That period also brought controversy. Jake’s online persona often attracted strong reactions, and his move into boxing was initially viewed by some people as another extension of his internet career rather than a serious sporting ambition.The family connection, however, remained important to Jake’s story.He has often been linked professionally and personally with Logan, whose own career later moved into boxing and WWE.Reflecting on his roots and his relationship with Logan, Jake said:“My brother and I came from nothing in Ohio. We were just two kids making videos in our backyard. Through all the noise, the hate, and the crazy world we stepped into, Logan has always been my partner in crime. I fight for my family, and no matter what anyone says, we built this together.”That quote needs to be checked against the original source before publication because I could not independently locate a reliable public transcript containing those exact words.Jake Paul’s boxing story began in 2018, but there is an important distinction between his first boxing appearance and his professional career.He fought Deji Olatunji in a white-collar boxing match in August 2018 and won by technical knockout. His professional debut came later, in January 2020, when he stopped AnEsonGib in the first round.From there, Jake started taking boxing more seriously. His opponents gradually became more experienced, including former UFC champion Tyron Woodley, former MMA champion Ben Askren, Anderson Silva and Nate Diaz. He also fought Tommy Fury in 2023 and lost by split decision, giving him his first defeat as a professional boxer at that point.His biggest mainstream boxing event came in November 2024, when he faced Mike Tyson in a Netflix fight. Paul won the bout by unanimous decision. In 2025, he added another win over former WBC middleweight champion Julio César Chávez Jr. before suffering his first professional stoppage loss against Anthony Joshua in December 2025.The change from internet creator to professional boxer did not happen overnight. It required Jake to spend years training and building a team around his boxing career.Explaining what the sport meant to him, Jake said:“People thought this was a joke or a publicity stunt. But boxing saved my life. It gave me structure, discipline, and purpose. I put in the work behind closed doors every single day when nobody is watching. You can’t fake it in that ring.”Again, this exact quote was supplied for the story but could not be independently verified through the public sources checked for this article.Even as Jake’s career expanded, his family remained closely connected to his public life. Logan Paul has been part of the same combat-sports world, while Jake’s parents have also featured in discussions about his upbringing and career.Jake is also engaged to Dutch speed skater Jutta Leerdam. The couple made their relationship public in 2023 and announced their engagement in March 2025. Leerdam has continued to pursue her own sporting career while supporting Jake.That gives Jake’s story a different side from the one usually seen through fight promotions and social media. His career is built around public attention, but he has repeatedly connected his personal goals with the people around him.Jake described that support this way:“At the end of the day, when the lights turn off and the cameras go away, family is all you have. My team and my family are my rock. Everything I do, every fight I take, is to build a legacy for my family and protect the people I love.”The wording should also be checked against the original source before publication. The available material supports the broader point that family has been an important part of Jake’s life, but not this exact quotation.Jake Paul’s rise is unusual because boxing was not where his fame began. He already had a large online audience before stepping into the ring. That gave him a platform, but it also meant he entered boxing with a reputation that many traditional fans did not take seriously.Instead of leaving the sport after the early criticism, he kept competing. His record now includes wins over several established names from combat sports, as well as defeats against Tommy Fury and Anthony Joshua. He also launched Most Valuable Promotions with adviser Nakisa Bidarian in 2021, giving him a role in boxing beyond being a fighter.His path has never been free from criticism. Some boxing fans continue to question the level and timing of his opponents, while others point to the attention and money his events have brought to the sport. Both reactions have become part of the Jake Paul story.His final message in the supplied material captures the idea behind his journey:Jake Paul built an empire by disrupting expectations and stepping into the ring, but his greatest strength remains his family foundation. By turning public doubt into motivation and staying loyal to his roots, he proves that true success belongs to those brave enough to fight for their own path.Jake Paul’s story is therefore less about a clean move from one career to another and more about constant reinvention. He first built an audience online, then used that attention to enter boxing and eventually became a promoter as well as a fighter. His career remains controversial, but the work he has put into boxing has made it much harder to describe him simply as a YouTuber who decided to fight.
Article Summary: Jake Paul turned internet fame into a boxing career. The Ohio-born creator moved from Vine and YouTubeinto professional boxing. He has faced former MMA champions, a former NBA player and Mike Tyson. His rise has also come with plenty of criticism, but boxing gave him a new way to build his identity.

Article Title: ‘Mujhe Narendra naam se nafrat ho gayi hai’: Narender Berwal’s Pakistan boxer story leaves PM Modi laughing

Narender Berwal and PM Narendra Modi (Video grabs)

Jadumani's Kargil connection

NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer's unusual reaction after losing to Indian heavyweight Narender Berwal left Prime Minister Narendra Modi amused during an interaction with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medallists on Sunday.Berwal, who won silver in the men's 90+kg category in Glasgow, recalled an incident from his boxing career when he defeated a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games. The boxer said his opponent was left bewildered by the repeated appearance of the name 'Narender' in his life.Recalling the exchange with Modi, Berwal said: “Pakistani boxer said to me, 'Aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narendra hai. Mujhe Narendra naam se nafrat ho gayi hai'...”The anecdote was part of a light-hearted interaction between Modi and India's medal winners at his residence in New Delhi. The Prime Minister congratulated the athletes for their performances and heard them recount some of the most memorable moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Berwal's silver was part of India's historic boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games.The Indian boxers returned from Glasgow with 10 medals, including seven golds and three silvers — their best-ever haul at the Games.India finished fourth overall in Glasgow with 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — despite competing in a smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme.Another boxer, Jadumani Singh, shared a more emotional story from Glasgow, recalling his victory over a Pakistani opponent on Kargil Vijay Diwas Jadumani, who won silver in the men's 55kg category, defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman 5-0 in the round of 16. Speaking to Modi, the boxer, who is associated with the Indian Army, explained why the date made the victory particularly significant.“It was Kargil Day. The day I fought against Pakistan was on that day. Being from the Indian Army, I was very determined that I had to beat Pakistan. I defeated them 5-0 and dedicated it to our Indian Army heroes,” Jadumani said.Modi praised the significance of the victory and its dedication to the Kargil heroes.“Remembering that, especially since you are from the forces yourself... I truly believe the sentiment you expressed, dedicating your medal to the Kargil winners, added extra glory to that victory. And you defeated exactly the one you were supposed to!” Modi said.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days of competition, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India, which will host the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.
Article Summary: Narender Berwal won silver in the men's 90+kg category at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Berwal said his opponent was left bewildered by the repeated appearance of the name 'Narendra' in his life. The anecdote was part of a light- hearted interaction between Modi and India's medal winners at his residence in Delhi.

Article Title: Imported machines, non-toxic gel, double-door entries and monkey whisperers: How Delhi is bracing for BWF World Championships
Article Text:
The Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium will host the BWF World Championships from August 17 in New Delhi. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

New Delhi:

Machines from the US have been brought in to tackle pigeons during the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Glass doors have been installed at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi as part of the infrastructural overhaul. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

The Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi has received a fresh coat of paint, new infrastructure, and swanky lights ahead of the BWF World Championships , which return to India after a 17-year gap. The objective is to host the best in world badminton, administrators from around the planet, thousands of fans and multiple VIPs starting August 17. The objective is also to ensure the pigeons and monkeys stay away, avoiding a repeat of the chaos at the India Open, earlier this year.In January, during the India Open, pigeons halted play in the match between HS Prannoy and Loh Kean Yew. Denmark's Mia Blichfeldt strongly criticised the practice and warm-up facility's hygiene. She complained about dirty areas and bird droppings near the training courts.While the Badminton Association of India (BAI) refuted the allegations, they and the Sports Authority of India (SAI), alongside the Sports Ministry, are leaving no stone unturned in ensuring something similar doesn't happen again.Wooden doors have given way to a double-door entry system in order to keep the monkeys away from entering the four-court premises and the training facilities at the KD Jadhav Stadium. Vents have been sealed to keep the pigeons from entering. Additionally, six plug-and-play machines have been imported from the US and installed to emit noise made by predatory birds. Further, non-toxic gel has also been filled in the roof ducts.The wheels for the preparations began as early as February, with things picking up pace in May. Hundreds of workers and contractors from the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) have been busy at work for the past few weeks to bring the tournament to fruition."The order for the pigeon gel went out in April, and it was imported only recently; it arrives in 10 days. It is a plug-and-play machine and can be imported from one stadium to another," said a source tracking developments to TimesofIndia.com."The only hiccup is that it can't be used at one place for a long period. The pigeons get accustomed to it and understand that this is not natural. But in the last 15-20 days of tests, it has worked well," he added.The gel in use is castor oil-based and has been installed on the surface of the root at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. Every time a bird sits on the top of the arena, it'll slip, ensuring they stay away.Another challenge for the organisers in the past has been monkeys. A full-grown rhesus macaque roamed the upper tier of the stands during the India Open. Now, as part of a Rs 20 crore revamp, 16 entrances have been fitted with glass doors and an automatic double-entry system.And if all else fails, a four-man team, led by Delhi-native Jabbar, is on hand to make noises similar to that of a langur to fend off monkeys. Born into a family of professional monkey whisperers, Jabbar, who earns Rs 25,000 a month, is confident that his and his team's vocal cords will be enough to keep monkeys at bay.
Article Summary: The Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi has received a fresh coat of paint, new infrastructure, and swanky lights. The objective is to host the best in world badminton, administrators from around the planet, thousands of fans and multiple VIPs starting August 17. In January, pigeons halted play in the match between HS Prannoy and Loh Kean Yew.

Article Title: Stefon Diggs' fresh start takes an ugly turn after devastating Commanders injury
Article Text:
Stefon Diggs is a father of six children in 2026 (Getty Images)

Stefon Diggs gave the Commanders hope; Laremy Tunsil's triceps took it away.

The low: Tunsil goes down, and it's not minor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A team that can't seem to get a full deck

For exactly three days, everything about the Washington Commanders' offseason made sense. They'd landed a genuine No. 2 receiver, Jayden Daniels finally had real weapons around him, and the vibes across training camp were as good as they'd been all summer. Then Saturday practice happened, and the whole storyline flipped.Diggs' free agency saga had dragged for months. The Patriots released him in March purely for cap relief, even though he'd just led their receiving corps to a Super Bowl appearance. Washington waited him out, and on August 5, it paid off.Diggs signed a one-year deal worth up to $12 million, and the team made it official two days later. For a guy from Gaithersburg, Maryland, it was framed as him coming home, and for the Commanders, it was framed as exactly the piece missing next to Terry McLaurin.Behind those two, the depth chart had been thin: Treylon Burks, Luke McCaffrey, a rookie. Diggs instantly became the best receiver not named McLaurin on the roster, and gave Daniels a second real threat defenses actually had to respect.For a team that went 12-5 with an NFC Championship run in 2024, then collapsed to 5-12 in 2025 largely because of injuries, the Diggs deal read like exactly the kind of aggressive, no-nonsense move that had defined Washington's whole offseason approach.Add it to trading for left tackle Laremy Tunsil back in March 2025, and this looked like a front office building something real.Then Saturday came. During a one-on-one pass rush rep against Odafe Oweh, Tunsil tried to stop a bull rush, the two locked up, and Tunsil awkwardly disengaged, immediately grabbing his arm in obvious pain.The diagnosis: a torn triceps. He'll need surgery, and the recovery window for that injury typically runs four to seven months, meaning Washington's best offensive lineman, a five-time Pro Bowler who'd just become the NFL's first $30-million-a-year tackle five months earlier, is likely out for most, if not all, of the 2026 season.The timing is almost cruel. Tunsil was PFF's sixth-ranked tackle in the league last year, allowing just two sacks and 15 pressures the entire season. He was the only Commander named to ESPN's top-10 players survey heading into this year. And he was supposed to be the guy keeping Daniels upright after a 2025 season where Daniels himself missed 10 games to three separate injuries.Washington's internal options to replace him aren't great. Andrew Wylie has played almost exclusively right tackle for his whole career. Brandon Coleman, who'd been competing for a starting guard spot, is the most likely candidate to slide out to tackle; he started 12 games there back in 2024, so it's not unfamiliar territory, but it's also not Tunsil.So here's where the Commanders sit: a receiving corps that looks genuinely dangerous for the first time in years, and an offensive line that just lost its best piece before the season's even started. One signing bought them a week of optimism. One practice rep took it right back.
Article Summary: Stefon Diggs signed a one-year deal worth up to $12 million with the Washington Commanders. The Patriots released him in March purely for cap relief. Diggs instantly became the best receiver not named McLaurin on the roster. Tunsil was PFF's sixth-ranked tackle in the league last year.

Article Title: What made Teddy Bridgewater retire again, right in the middle of training camp?
Article Text:
Teddy Bridgewater

Teddy Bridgewater just retired for the second time, and this one might actually stick

"I've known him a long time, and man, the human being is unbelievable,"

"Always played the game up here, pointing to his head, and had a huge heart. He's going to be missed."

This isn't actually his first goodbye

"I think he can only truly answer that, but I feel like this is where it's at for sure right now,"

"This is where it needs to be."

A twelve-year run through seven teams

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Teddy Bridgewater is walking away from football again, and this time it happened in the middle of training camp with almost no warning. The veteran quarterback informed the Detroit Lions on Sunday that he's stepping away from the team, with retirement expected to follow. It's not the first time he's done this. It might be the last.Bridgewater, 33, was in Detroit competing for the backup job behind starter Jared Goff on a one-year, $1.8 million deal he'd signed this offseason. Then, with camp underway, he simply told the team he was done.Lions head coach Dan Campbell broke the news to reporters before Sunday's practice, and didn't hide how much it stung.Campbell said.The Lions placed Bridgewater on the reserve/retired list that same day and moved fast to fill the hole, signing Josh Dobbs shortly after.Here's the part that makes this retirement different from a standard career sendoff: Bridgewater already did this once before. He first retired in February 2024, after a lone appearance for Detroit the year prior, and used the time away to coach his old high school team, Miami Northwestern, to a state championship.That chapter took an odd turn when he was suspended over allegations of providing improper benefits to players, something he later said he didn't regret. Then, just months later, the pull of the league brought him back. He signed with Detroit again in December 2024 and stuck around through this year's camp.Campbell doesn't think there's a third act coming this time.Campbell said.However you count the gap in the middle, Bridgewater's NFL story stretches back to 2014, when the Vikings took him 32nd overall out of Louisville.He started strong with an 11-5 record and a playoff berth in his second season, before a brutal training camp knee injury in 2016 nearly ended his career before it really got going. He fought back from that, then spent the rest of his career bouncing between teams: the Jets, Saints, Panthers, Broncos, Dolphins, and finally Detroit, seven stops in all, mostly in backup and bridge-starter roles.It's not a career full of Pro Bowls or highlight reels. It's a career built on staying ready, adjusting to seven different rosters, and coming back from an injury that could've ended things at 24. That's arguably a harder thing to pull off than stardom, and it's why even a quiet, mid-camp exit like this one is getting the kind of respect usually reserved for much bigger names.
Article Summary: Teddy Bridgewater announced his retirement from the NFL on Sunday. It's not the first time he's done this, and it might not be the last. The 33-year-old spent 12 years in the NFL, playing for seven different teams.

The Sick Mind of EDP445

Who is EDP445 and what happened in the 2021 sting?

What does Mike Clum’s The Sick Mind of EDP445 reveal about Bryant Moreland?

Bryant Moreland, better known as EDP445, is back in focus after Mike Clum’s documentaryrevisits the controversy that ended his YouTube career. Released on YouTube on August 9, the film looks at Moreland’s rise, the 2021 sting involving a decoy he believed was a 13-year-old girl, and his life now. One of the most striking claims comes from Moreland himself: he says ‘God saved him’ from arrest during another alleged situation involving someone he believed was a minor. The documentary also introduces his girlfriend, Marissa, and shares details about their relationship.Bryant Moreland became famous as EDP445 through loud, unfiltered videos about the Philadelphia Eagles. His channel later included food videos, vlogs, reactions and personal rants. At his peak, he had more than two million YouTube subscribers and also appeared on. His online name is linked to a profanity-based phrase, which is why it is better known today simply as EDP445.His career changed in April 2021. A predator-catching group confronted Moreland in Bakersfield, California, after he had exchanged sexually explicit messages with a decoy posing as a 13-year-old girl. Moreland had gone to meet the person and, during the confrontation, said, “I was actually coming out here to pick up a cupcake.”The line became the centre of the controversy and later turned into a major internet meme.YouTube then terminated his channels. Moreland was not criminally charged over that particular sting. The lack of charges did not restore his career, and his later attempts to return to online platforms kept his name tied to the same controversy.The new documentary gives Moreland a long chance to speak about his past and current life. It includes interviews, recreations and appearances from people connected to his story, including Chris Hansen.One of the film’s most talked-about moments is Moreland’s claim that God prevented him from being arrested during another alleged incident involving someone he believed was underage. The documentary presents the claim as Moreland’s account; it does not establish that any divine intervention took place. That distinction matters because the 2021 sting itself did not lead to criminal charges.The film also turns to Moreland’s relationship with Marissa. He introduces her as his girlfriend and says they have been together for more than a year. Marissa describes him as a “genuine great guy” with a “huge heart”. Moreland says “they have not had sex” and talks about his frustration with the lack of physical intimacy.The film does not change the basic record of the 2021 case. Moreland’s statements are his own account, while the earlier sting footage and the platform ban remain the key public facts. That makes the documentary more about his version of events and present-day life than a new criminal case.Clum has said the documentary is not meant to rehabilitate Moreland. He also said its cinematic style reflects his own filmmaking approach. The project is free on YouTube, and Clum said its proceeds are being directed to RAINN, a sexual assault support organisation.

Baker Mayfield’s future in Tampa Bay could become one of the NFL’s more intriguing contract stories after the 2026 season. The Buccaneers quarterback wants to stay, but Mike Florio believes a failed long-term deal could push him toward an unexpected AFC destination. Florio has identified the Pittsburgh Steelers as a particularly strong fit, even suggesting Mayfield might accept less money to leave Tampa Bay if the situation turns sour. That possibility adds another layer to negotiations that have already stalled, especially with Mayfield entering the final year of his current contract and set to hit free agency in 2027.Baker Mayfield has already made his preference clear. His family is settled in Tampa, and he wants to continue playing for the Buccaneers. The problem is the length of the contract, rather than simply the money.According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Tampa Bay offered Mayfield a two-year extension worth around $50 million annually. Mayfield, however, was looking for more years. That gap could become important if the quarterback enters 2027 without a new deal.Florio believes Mayfield’s personality could make the situation even more interesting.The quarterback has responded strongly to perceived slights before, and Florio pointed back to his time with Cleveland.“Baker Mayfield is no different than the guy that he was when he was drafted first overall by the Browns in 2018, and they pissed him off,” Florio said on the “Pardon My Take” podcast. “And what happens when you piss off Baker Mayfield?”Florio then raised the possibility of Mayfield deliberately choosing a different path.“He could take less, just as a middle finger to the Buccaneers for not paying him when they had the chance,” Florio said.That is where Pittsburgh enters the picture.Florio sees the Steelers as more than a random alternative. He called Pittsburgh a “perfect” destination and suggested Mayfield could value the fit enough to leave money on the table.“I could see him taking less money to go to Pittsburgh, to some other — like, Pittsburgh is the perfect — it just feels like the perfect destination for him.”The timing could also make the Steelers an interesting option. Aaron Rodgers has already said 2026 will be his final season, potentially leaving Pittsburgh searching for its next starting quarterback.Mayfield will have plenty to prove before that decision arrives. He completed 343 of 543 passes for 3,693 yards, 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 17 starts during the 2025 regular season while playing through injuries.His QB Impact Metric from PFN dropped to 74.4, ranking 22nd, after an 86.1 score and fourth-place ranking in 2024. Still, Mayfield has a history of responding when his future is uncertain.“The other part of this is the Bucs and the entire NFL have seen what Baker Mayfield can do when he’s got something to prove, when his back is against the wall,” Rapoport said.That may be the biggest factor heading into 2026. If Mayfield performs like he did in his stronger Tampa Bay season, the Buccaneers may have to revisit their position quickly. If they do not, Pittsburgh could become a genuine option rather than just Florio’s intriguing prediction.

Article Title: How Travis Kelce's kindness to a family he'd never met helped Laila Edwards make history on Olympic ice

When the United States women's hockey team lifted gold at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan-Cortina, Laila Edwards was right in the middle of it. The 22-year-old defender from Cleveland Heights, Ohio, had just played a central role in one of the most celebrated moments in recent American hockey history. But speaking to San Jose Sharks broadcaster Brodie Brazil this week, Edwards revealed something most people never knew that Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce , whose net worth sits at an estimated $90 million, had quietly backed her dream long before she ever stepped onto Olympic ice.It started with a Twitter DM from her father.Years before Edwards was a household name, she was just a teenager trying to fund a summer hockey tournament overseas. Her family didn't have the money, so they ran a small fundraiser and her dad decided to shoot his shot. He messaged Travis Kelce directly, asking him to donate to his daughter's fund."I don't think I have ever told this story, but years ago, I was trying to go overseas for like a little hockey tournament in the summer, and we just didn't have the money, so we did a little fundraiser, and my dad direct messaged Travis on Twitter like 'hey donate to my daughter's fund… blah blah blah,' and he donated $100 and I was like wow," Edwards said.That could have been the end of it -- a one-time gesture from a celebrity who would never cross her path again. But then, in November 2023, Edwards made history as the first Black woman to play for the U.S. women's national hockey team. The Kelce brothers gave her a shoutout on their widely popular New Heights podcast.She sent them a message, fully expecting it to disappear into a celebrity inbox, never to be read. Travis replied."Fast forward where I make the USA team, and they shout me out on their podcast, and I thought that was pretty cool. So I just messaged them knowing they would never see it, and Travis got back to me, and we had a good conversation. He was asking about my past blah blah. We were wishing each other luck, rooting for each other… all that good stuff," Edwards recalled.By the time the 2026 Olympics came around, their connection had grown into something more concrete. Edwards' family set up a GoFundMe to cover flights and accommodation in Milan so her parents, siblings, grandmother, and other relatives could watch her compete. Travis and his brother Jason donated.Edwards didn't put a figure on it during the interview, but she made clear the contribution was substantial. "Then we started GoFundMe, and Travis donates, and that was just… he donated a very great portion that helped my family, everyone get over there without like the financial worries. And having my family there meant the world, they're the reason I got there," she said.According to the NHL, Travis and Jason Kelce donated $10,000 to the GoFundMe. The family had set a target of $50,000. They ultimately raised over $61,000 — enough to bring 14 family members to Milan, including Edwards' 91-year-old grandmother, who shared a pre-game ritual with her from the stands throughout the tournament.Edwards spoke warmly about both brothers, describing them as people whose character runs deeper than their public profile. She said she came to realize that neither Travis nor Jason is driven by fame or money -- they're just genuinely good people.It's a detail that adds a quieter dimension to Kelce's public persona. The $100 donation to an unknown teenager's fundraiser years ago wasn't a calculated PR moment. Neither was the $10,000 to make sure that same teenager -- now an Olympic gold medalist, got to celebrate with her family in Italy.
Article Summary: Laila Edwards, 22, is the first Black woman to play for the U.S. women's hockey team. Travis Kelce donated $100 to a teenager's fundraiser years ago. Kelce and his brother Jason donated $10,000 to Edwards' GoFundMe.

The two takes frame very different pictures of where Curry's future stands.The Stephen Curry trade rumor making the rounds this offseason has no basis, according to ClutchPoints insider Brett Siegel. Curry has stayed with the Warriors since he arrived in 2009, and speculation about his future picked up after Golden State missed on top targets including Giannis Antetokounmpo, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this summer.Siegel shut that talk down on the Clutch Scoops podcast, saying there is zero truth to rumors that Curry could request a trade from Golden State. He added that the belief inside the organization is unequivoca, "The biggest part of everything, because there's just rumors going out of nowhere, Tomer, about, 'Oh, Steph Curry's going to be traded, he's going to request a trade,' None of that is true," Siegel said, citing what he described as extremely good authority from within the Warriors that Curry intends to stay for the rest of his career.Siegel added, "Steph Curry is not going to be requesting a trade. We have that on extremely good authority from the Warriors that Steph Curry is staying there; he wants to remain there his entire career, and this extension is basically going to lock him in for that."That framing matters because Curry has never publicly pushed for a move, even during the franchise's rebuilding stretch two seasons ago. The front office's recent swings at star talent were about building around him, not preparing for his exit.Curry becomes extension eligible on August 29, and Golden State can put a two-year, $136.7 million deal in front of him. He argued the Warriors can close out games once they get to crunch time, but doubted their ability to consistently reach that point.Russell went on to picture Curry alongside Jayson Tatum and Paul George in Boston, calling the pairing something he would want to watch. He also noted Curry has spent his entire NBA career inside one system, aside from Team USA duty, and said seeing him adapt somewhere else would be worth watching in its own right.Whether that scenario ever becomes real is a separate question. For now, the extension talks point toward Curry staying exactly where he has always been.

Simone Biles is known around the world for her Olympic success. But behind the medals is a childhood that was far from easy. The organisation gives children something Biles knows can change a life: a trusted adult who stays by their side.Simone Biles spent three years in the Houston-area foster care system after her biological mother struggled with substance use. Her grandparents, Ron and Nellie Biles, later took care of her and eventually adopted her.Years later, Biles helped bring Friends of the Children to Houston. The organisation pairs children with professional mentors who make a 12-year commitment to them. The goal is simple. Children should have someone they can trust as they grow up.Tre Maxie, executive director of Friends of the Children-Houston, explained why Biles has such a strong connection with the programme in a Stand Together interview.“One of the exciting things about Simone bringing Friends to Houston, which is her hometown, is her background as a foster kid.She can relate to a lot of our kids who are either foster kids or have some instabilities in their life. To have a model where you have community members raise their hand and say, ‘I want to work with this kid for 12 years,’ it’s tremendous. It has the potential to really transform the lives of some of our children, who have more challenges than any person should have, much less a child. ”That is what makes Biles’ involvement different. She is not simply supporting a cause from the outside. She knows what it feels like when a child’s life changes because of the adults around them.The Houston chapter started in 2023. Its first group included 24 children between the ages of 4 and 6, along with three mentors. Those mentors are expected to remain part of the children’s lives for 12 years.Biles has also spoken about the importance of having someone believe in you. During a Friends of the Children event, she said:“I love Friends of the Children so much because you guys have mentors, your Friends, who believe in you, and that you can do anything you put your minds to.”Simone Biles’ work with the organisation has also gained attention through her Olympic journey. During the Paris Olympics, Friends of the Children held watch events at the World Champions Centre, where Biles trained, giving local children a chance to watch her compete.For those children, Biles represents more than Olympic medals. Her story shows them that their starting point does not have to decide where they finish.Biles has never hidden her connection to foster children. In a Vanity Fair interview, she said:“I’ll always advocate for foster kids. I was a foster kid and something very out of the ordinary happened to me.”She also spoke about bringing the organisation to Houston, saying:“We’re opening a chapter in Houston. I think the kids deserve that.”That belief remains at the heart of her work. Biles knows that not every child will become an Olympic champion. But with the right support, they can still discover what they are capable of.Her gymnastics career gave her a global platform. Now, she is using that platform to make sure children facing difficult beginnings know they can dream beyond them.

Jake Whisenant's cause of death has been determined by the Tulare County Sheriff's Office Coroner Unit, which lists the manner as accidental after the record-breaking climber fell during an ascent in the Sierra Nevada on Aug. 3. The sheriff's office covers Tulare County, which includes Sequoia National Park and stretches into the southern Sierra Nevada, and its coroner unit is the agency of record for the case.The National Park Service separately confirmed the incident occurred within Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, telling SFGATE that a search-and-rescue operation began Aug.2, a day before Whisenant's death was confirmed.
